title: Police file murder raps vs 6 people over killing of working student in Batangas
content:
Six individuals are facing a murder complaint over the killing of a 22-year-old working student in San Jose, Batangas, according to the municipal police.
San Jose Municipal Police Station (MPS) on Monday said it filed a murder complaint against four identified respondents and two unidentified individuals in connection with the killing of Charles Usi.
“The complaint was filed on October 29, 2026, before the Office of the Batangas Provincial Prosecutor at Bulwagang Katarungan, Batangas City, under Docket No. IV-02-PE-26J-00281 for violation of Article 248 of the Revised Penal Code, as amended,” the police said.
San Jose MPS identified the four identified respondents by their aliases "Xam," "Ento," "Non," and "Dali."
All six respondents remain at large, according to the San Jose MPS.
Earlier, the Philippine National Police (PNP) confirmed that a well-known personality and five other individuals were linked to Usi’s death.
Investigators were looking into a possible love triangle as the motive behind the killing.
The victim was shot dead while riding his motorcycle along the national highway in Barangay Banay-banay II on October 25.
Video footage showed the victim traveling along the highway when unidentified suspects riding another motorcycle allegedly pulled alongside him and opened fire.
Police initially thought the victim had figured in a road accident. However, responding personnel later discovered that he had sustained gunshot wounds to the back that pierced through his chest.
He was rushed to a hospital but was declared dead.
Investigators recovered two empty shell casings from a .45-caliber firearm at the crime scene.
Authorities said the victim was reportedly on his way home from the restaurant where he worked as a musician when the shooting happened. — RSJ, GMA News

title: Mayon Volcano emits ash anew
content:
Mayon Volcano in Albay emitted ash on Tuesday morning, according to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS).
In an update, PHIVOLCS said the ash emission started at 8:22 a.m.
“This event generated a plume that rose 1600 meters above the summit crater before drifting southwest, as recorded by the Mayon Volcano Observatory Ligñon Hill (VMLH) and the Ligao Observation Station (VMLI) IP Cameras,” PHIVOLCS said.
Alert Level 3 remains in effect over the volcano, indicating an increased tendency toward a hazardous eruption.
Mayon Volcano has been under Alert Level 3 since October 30, when it experienced a moderately explosive eruption.
The initial eruption generated a grayish plume that rose approximately 3,000 meters above the crater and drifted west-southwest.
PHIVOLCS has recommended the evacuation in the six-kilometer Permanent Danger Zone (PDZ) due to the threat of pyroclastic density currents (PDCs), lava flows, rockfalls, and other volcanic hazards.
Civil aviation authorities were advised to warn pilots against flying close to Mayon's summit, as volcanic ash from sudden eruptions could pose a hazard to aircraft.
On Monday, PHIVOLCS also reported a minor eruption at Mayon's summit crater.

title: PNP bares possible charges in dumping of animal remains in Bulacan
content:
The Philippine National Police (PNP) on Tuesday bared the possible criminal charges against those responsible for the dumping of remains of 29 dogs and cats in a vacant lot in San Jose del Monte, Bulacan.
In a statement, the PNP said those who may be held liable could face the following cases:
- estafa under Article 315(2)(a) of the Revised Penal Code
- syndicated estafa
- violations of the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines
- violations of the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act
- violations of the Consumer Act of the Philippines
Affected customers may also pursue civil claims for damages.
The decomposing remains of dogs and cats were found sealed in plastic bags and dumped along a road in Barangay Minuyan Proper in San Jose del Monte.
The animal remains were allegedly dumped following a suspected fraudulent operation involving a pet crematorium in Bacoor City, Cavite.
PNP chief Police General Jose Melencio Nartatez Jr. urged pet owners who may have been victimized by the establishment to formally file complaints and submit evidence.
Affected customers are advised to preserve and submit receipts, cremation certificates, transaction records, and other relevant documents that could help establish possible violations of the law.
Nartatez directed police units in Bulacan and Cavite to coordinate with other law enforcement agencies and assist in identifying the individuals who allegedly transported and dumped the animal remains.
Investigators are examining the establishment's business permits, equipment, CCTV footage, and procedures for handling pets entrusted to the facility.
Forensic examinations will also be conducted to determine whether the recovered remains belonged to animals brought to the crematorium and whether the ashes returned to their owners were authentic.
Concerned police offices were also directed to coordinate with barangay officials and local government units to secure and review CCTV footage along the suspected route of the white van reportedly used in the dumping.
"Any form of deception that exploits the trust of grieving pet owners is deeply concerning and must be addressed with the full force of the law," Nartatez said. —VAL, GMA News

title: PDP-Laban holds indignation rally outside SC for Rodrigo Duterte, Bato dela Rosa
content:
Despite rainy weather, members and supporters of political party Partido Demokratiko Pilipino-Lakas ng Bayan (PDP-Laban) gathered outside the Supreme Court (SC) on Tuesday morning.
The group held an indignation rally calling for the swift resolution of cases involving former President Rodrigo Duterte and Senator Ronald "Bato” dela Rosa.
“Hindi alintana ang ulan, patuloy ang pagdating at pagtitipon ng mga kababayan natin sa harap ng Korte Suprema ngayong Martes ng umaga, November 3, para sa isang Indignation Rally,” PDP-Laban said.
(Despite the rain, our countrymen continue to arrive and gather in front of the Supreme Court this Tuesday morning, November 3, for an Indignation Rally.)
“Sa kabila ng masamang panahon, tuloy ang pagpapahayag ng kanilang paninindigan” it added.
(Despite the bad weather, they continue to express their stance.
PDP-Laban is set to submit a letter to the SC reiterating its appeal for an immediate ruling on the cases.
'Delays'
In an open letter issued on October 31 and signed by acting chairman Alfonso Cusi, the political party urged the SC to resolve the legal questions surrounding Duterte and Dela Rosa, saying prolonged delays could further fuel uncertainty and instability.
PDP-Laban questioned the alleged procedural delays in the cases, noting that a habeas corpus petition filed on behalf of Duterte had remained pending before the high tribunal for nearly 600 days.
It also called for the immediate resolution of Dela Rosa's pending motion for reconsideration.
Duterte was arrested by Philippine authorities in Pasay City and was handed over to the International Criminal Court (ICC) on March 11, 2025.
He was flown via a chartered plane to The Hague, where he will be tried for crimes against humanity in relation to his bloody war on drugs while he was mayor of Davao City and President of the Philippines.
The trial is scheduled to begin on November 30, 2026.
Dela Rosa is also wanted by the ICC as he is accused of being a co-perpetrator in the alleged crimes.
A P50-million reward is being offered for information that would lead to the senator’s arrest. —VAL, GMA News

title: ICC prosecutors want to admit 3 pre-recorded testimonies on Duterte's 'narco-list'
content:
PRAGUE, Czech Republic – To expedite the proceedings in Rodrigo Duterte’s case before the International Criminal Court (ICC), the Office of the Prosecutor seeks to admit three pre-recorded witness testimonies regarding the former President’s “narco list.”
In a redacted request for application filed on November 2, Acting Prosecutor Mame Mandiaye Niang requested Trial Chamber III to admit the prior recorded testimonies of witnesses P-1097, P-1170, and P-1318, which are “relevant” proof of Duterte’s “individual criminal liability”, particularly in identifying “high-value targets” on various drug watch lists.
The prosecution added that these statements also establish the Philippine National Police’s (PNP) role in Duterte’s drug war.
Niang stated that the prior recorded testimonies are introduced via the ICC’s Rule of Procedure and Evidence Rule 68(3), which may allow admission of such statements in proceedings while the witness appears in court and does not object.
Recorded testimonies
Although heavily redacted, the three witnesses’ statements, as the prosecution noted, establish the targeting of individuals by PNP officers during Duterte’s drug war, as well as “the shift in [REDACTED] after Mr Duterte became President.”
P-1097’s prior recorded testimony explains the “tokhang” killings and that “warning placards were placed on some victims.”
The prosecution noted that P-1170’s testimony demonstrates Duterte’s public accusation of redacted individuals as being involved with illegal drugs, who were later included on the “PRRD list.”
The pre-recorded testimony of P-1318 is heavily redacted, but the prosecution said it describes the Operation Double Barrel and the tokhang killings, including “some police killings [that] were staged through nanlaban narratives, evidence planting, and cover-ups.”
The prosecution noted that it would conduct a “limited and focused supplementary examination” of the witnesses – all referred to in the filing with male pronouns – should their prior recorded testimonies be introduced as evidence.
It also seeks to use associated materials for P-1097, P-1170, and P-1318 as evidence “necessary to fully comprehend” their accounts.
The filing noted that the three witnesses’ statements “are internally consistent, mutually corroborative, and accompanied by supporting documents in relation to certain aspects,” and that they corroborate the evidence to be provided by other viva voce witnesses.
'Paper-only' witness
Meanwhile, Duterte’s defense counsel, Peter Haynes, is asking Trial Chamber III to reject the prosecution’s application to admit witness P-1357’s prior recorded testimony under Rule 68(2), which would allow the statement in court without the witness’s appearance.
In a redacted response filing on the same day, Haynes claims P-1357 “exemplifies the very type of individual whom the Chamber urged the Prosecution to remove from its list.”
“Her testimony is entirely peripheral, as it does not address the substance of [REDACTED] research, the allegations made, or the findings reached. The witness is not even familiar with the events occurring after [REDACTED], having ceased working on the subject following [REDACTED],” Haynes stated.
It may be recalled that the prosecution asked Trial Chamber III on October 19 to admit the prior recorded testimony of P-1357, P-0024, and P-1359 as Rule 68(2)(b) evidence that relates to the alleged systematic policy of “neutralizing” alleged criminals across the Philippines through murder.
The prior recorded testimony of P-1357, referred to in female pronouns, contains details of the existence and operations of the Davao Death Squad and “notes that the words and actions of Mr Duterte indicated his support for killings of criminal suspects.”
But Haynes objected to admitting P-1357’s statement, saying it “adds nothing of substance to the evidence in this case.”
“Further and/or alternatively, the Defence objects to the Prosecution’s improper use of Rule 68(2)(b) to introduce associated material that the witness has neither meaningfully used nor explained, contrary to the Prosecution’s assertions,” Haynes stated.
Haynes said the defense has “no wish” to cross-examine P-1357, “given the marginal relevance of her testimony.”
The defense said it won’t cross-examine P-0024 because of “having already extensively addressed its concerns regarding the introduction of the [REDACTED] dataset into the evidentiary record of these proceedings.”
P-0024’s heavily redacted statement mentions a “legal process,” and “records [that] may have been incomplete or selectively disclosed.” It remains unclear which information P-0024’s statement refers to.
Ramifications, deadlines
At the final status conference, senior trial lawyer Julian Nicholls and trial lawyer Edward Jeremy told Trial Chamber III Presiding Judge Joanna Korner that the Office of the Prosecution would submit eight additional applications to admit Rule 68(3) witnesses.
Korner also asked the prosecution and the defense for suggestions on in-court protective measures regarding Rule 68(3) witnesses, citing “various ramifications” and the need for “certainty about the deadlines.”
Earlier, Nichols said that by submitting prior recorded witness statements, they hope to “cut down in half” the six hours allocated to present their opening statements.
The ICC’s trial of Duterte for crimes against humanity is set for November 30. —VAL, GMA News

title: EXPLAINER: ICC Rules 68.2 and 68.3: How prior witness testimonies may be used in Duterte trial
content:
THE HAGUE — Rules 68.2 and 68.3 of the International Criminal Court's (ICC) Rules of Procedure and Evidence were mentioned during the fifth and final status conference in the case of former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte on Monday.
The provisions concern the use of previously recorded witness testimony and this could affect how evidence is presented when Duterte's trial begins on November 30.
The key distinction between the two rules is whether the witness must appear before the Trial Chamber.
Under Rule 68.2, the court may allow previously recorded testimony to be introduced even if the witness is not present. This is permitted only under specific circumstances, including when both the prosecution and defense had the opportunity to examine the witness during the recording, or when the witness has died, is unavailable despite reasonable efforts, or has been subjected to improper interference.
The rule also allows the introduction of testimony concerning matters other than the accused's acts and conduct, subject to additional requirements.
Rule 68.3, meanwhile, applies when the witness is present before the Trial Chamber. Previously recorded testimony may be introduced if the witness does not object and the prosecution, defense and judges have the opportunity to examine them during the proceedings.
Atty. Kristina Conti, an ICC counsel representing the victims, explained that Rule 68.3 covers witnesses who already have recorded statements or other material on record.
“Ang ibig sabihin lang po nito, ang may 68.3, ito po ay mga witnesses na meron ng dating testimonya, dokumento o, ah, videos na sila'y nagsasalaysay. So kumbaga may affidavit na dati,” Conti said.
(What this means is that the 68.3 are witnesses who have previous testimonies, documents or, ah, videos of them giving their accounts. So there was an affidavit before.)
Conti said the existence of these materials could help shorten court proceedings because some of the witness's statements and supporting evidence have already been documented.
“Si 68.3, sisipot pa rin (68.3 will still show up),” she said, stressing that witnesses under this provision would still appear before the court.
For Rule 68.2, Conti explained: “Si 68.2, replacement of the testimony. Tanggapin yung testimonya nila pero hindi nasisipot yung witnesses (Their testimony is accepted but they will not appear).”
The use of previously recorded testimony may, however, be contested by the defense, which has raised concerns about its ability to question witnesses whose evidence is significant to the prosecution's case.
The defense has also pointed to the need to examine how certain reports and documents were produced, including the people involved in preparing them. It has indicated that it intends to present its own witnesses in response to the prosecution's evidence.
The Trial Chamber will ultimately decide whether a particular recorded testimony can be admitted under Rule 68 and whether the requirements have been met.
Duterte's trial is scheduled to begin on November 30. — BAP, GMA News

title: Trump says Iran deal 'could happen!'
content:

title: Vessel struck near Strait of Hormuz -- maritime agency
content:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates - British maritime agency UKMTO reported on Monday that a vessel was struck by "an unknown projectile" near the Strait of Hormuz a day earlier, marking the latest disturbance in the contested waterway.
The agency said the incident occurred on Sunday off the coast of Lima, Oman, around the mouth of the strait.
"The master reports the vessel has been struck by an unknown projectile which has caused a hole on the starboard side. Vessel and crew safe, no environmental impact reported," the agency said in a statement.
The Strait of Hormuz carried roughly 20 percent of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the Middle East war, which erupted with US-Israeli strikes on Iran in late February.
Since then, Tehran has placed a chokehold on the shipping route and regularly targets ships that pass without its authorization.
Washington has responded by maintaining a blockade on Iranian ports, and negotiations between the two countries are deadlocked.
Attacks on vessels attempting to cross the waterway have increased recently, as Washington escorts more ships through the strait and Tehran seeks to maintain control over their passage. — Agence France-Presse

title: New cyberattack on supermarket fridges sweeps across Europe
content:
STOCKHOLM/BRUSSELS/LONDON - A hacking attack on European supermarkets spread across the continent on Monday, hitting fridges and freezers from Sweden to Belgium and forcing stores to throw away food in an incident that echoed a similar attack in France last month.
The attack, which raised temperatures in refrigerator and freezer units at dozens of stores, hit supermarket groups Ahold Delhaize AD.AS and Colruyt COLR.BR in Belgium and Luxembourg, as well as Swedish grocers ICA and Coop. Furniture-to-meatballs retailer IKEA also saw at least one store affected.
"Everything is destroyed," Engla Ingwall, sales manager at an ICA franchise store in Stockholm, told Reuters during a visit to the store on Monday, adding the attack occurred at 2 a.m. (0100 GMT) but was only noticed hours later.
"There has been a cyberattack and all our freezers reached 50 degrees (Celsius)."
A spokesperson for privately held ICA said the company was aware that a "limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems".
The latest incidents follow an attack in France last month when police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, causing fires and food losses. Ahold also reported a cybersecurity incident to police last month.
While no one has claimed responsibility for either attack, the incidents have heightened concerns among European authorities about hybrid threats to infrastructure amid growing security tensions since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine.
Moscow has repeatedly denied involvement in sabotage or hybrid warfare operations. Reuters could not establish who was behind Monday's attacks or whether they were linked to the incidents in France.
"It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be determined," said Katrien Eggers, spokesperson for Belgium's Centre for Cybersecurity, adding she was concerned about the growing number of incidents, in part due to AI.
"All IT systems are potentially vulnerable, and AI can now be used to successfully exploit these weaknesses — especially by sophisticated actors," she said.
'Retail is an easy target'
From refrigerators and heating systems to security cameras and alarms, an expanding range of devices once largely mechanical can now be monitored and controlled remotely, creating new opportunities for cybercriminals.
At least some of the refrigerator units affected on Monday used temperature control technology from Danish firm Danfoss that was also targeted in the French attack. The firm said it had been working with customers to implement fixes.
The European Commission said the latest incidents highlighted how digital threats are becoming increasingly disruptive.
"They are a deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain and undermine consumers' confidence in it – a warning that we must take seriously," said EU commissioner for agriculture Christophe Hansen. "The repeated occurrence of these cyberattacks is deeply concerning."
A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops had their fridge systems attacked.
In Ireland, wholesaler Musgrave said the incident affected systems in 13 of its SuperValu stores, forcing it to remove some chilled and frozen products from sale.
"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue and we took immediate action," it said in a statement. "Our investigation is ongoing."
Tom Hegel, a researcher at cybersecurity firm SentinelOne, said such attacks were typically linked to extortion, political motives or nation-state operations, with the absence of financial demands in recent cases pointing instead to sabotage.
"Retail is an easy target because retail chains run enormous estates of refrigeration controllers, building management systems, door access panels and point-of-sale gear," he said, adding it was hard to trace hackers targeting such systems.
"An attacker who logs into an exposed control panel leaves almost nothing behind ... A teenager and an intelligence service would look much the same from the defender's side."
'It's very scary'
Carrefour CARR.PA, which was badly hit in last month's French attack, said 15 of its 700 stores in Belgium were affected. IKEA said one store in Belgium had been impacted and that it could not rule out disruptions at other locations.
Privately held Swedish grocery chain Coop said that 7 of its 800 stores were affected by a cyber incident involving unauthorized tampering with its refrigeration systems. It said Danfoss was among its suppliers.
Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery chain De Laet & Van Haver, said he was woken at 3:30 a.m. by an employee telling him there was a problem. He rushed to his store south of Antwerp and found the fridges turned up as high as 18 C.
He estimated the incident ruined about €15,000 ($16,800) worth of meat.
"It's very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance," he told Reuters, adding that it was infuriating to throw away so much food.
De Laet said he believed the hackers were trying to destabilize European economies. He had contacted police but did not know whether an investigation had been launched.
"I only have two words for them: wake up, please, because there's something going on," he said. ($1 = 0.8948 euros) — Reuters

title: 2 patay sa sunog sa Barangay E. Rodriguez, Quezon City
content:
Dalawa ang kumpirmadong patay sa sunog na sumiklab sa Barangay E. Rodriguez, Quezon City, ayon sa Quezon City Fire District (QCFD).

title: Off-duty na pulis na umano'y lasing, kinuyog ng mga lalaki na kaniyang sinita nang makitang may dala siyang baril
content:
Sa ospital ang bagsak ng isang pulis matapos siyang kuyugin ng ilang lalaki na kaniyang sinita sa gilid ng daan sa Antipolo, Rizal. Ang pulis, off-duty, nakasibilyan at lasing umano nang mangyari ang insidente, ayon sa ilang saksi.
Sa ulat ni EJ Gomez sa GMA News “24 Oras” nitong Lunes, sinabing nangyari ang insidente sa Barangay San Jose noong Sabado ng madaling araw.
Sa video footage, madidinig ang boses ng isang lalaki na nagsabing biglang tumigil sa kanila ang lalaking nakasakay sa motorsiklo at nagpakilalang pulis.
Madidinig sa video na may nagsabi na papasok na sila sa gate at magliligpit na ng kanilang gamit.
Ngunit nagpatuloy pa ang usapan hanggang sa hawakan na ang kamay ng nagpakilalang pulis nang makita na mayroon siyang baril, hanggang sa mauwi na ito sa pagkakagulpi sa pulis.
Dinala sa ospital ang lalaki na nagtamo ng sugat sa mukha. Nakumpirma naman ng pulisya na kabaro talaga nila ang lalaki na may ranggong Corporal.
Sa imbestigasyon ng pulisya, nag-iinuman umano ang sinita nitong grupo ng mga lalaki, pero itinanggi ito ng saksi sa pangyayari.
Ayon sa saksi, naglalaro ng online games ang mga kalalakihan nang dumaan ang lalaking nagpakilalang pulis na sakay ng motorsiklo at nangungursunada umano.
Hindi rin umano makausap nang maayos ang nagpakilalang pulis dahil sa pagiging lasing.
Kinuyog umano ng mga lalaki ang nagpakilalang pulis dahil sa pag-aakala nilang mamamaril na ito nang makita nila ang baril.
Apat na sangkot sa insidente ang inaresto ng mga pulis, at nasa dalawang menor de edad ang nasa Lingap Kabataan.
Sinusubukan pang makuhanan ng pahayag ang nagpapagaling na pulis. – FRJ GMA News

title: Duterte ICC trial: Victims face language barriers, concerns over scope of charges
content:
THE HAGUE, Netherlands — Victims of alleged crimes committed during former president Rodrigo Duterte's war on drugs face challenges in participating meaningfully in his upcoming trial before the International Criminal Court (ICC), including language barriers, witness protection concerns, and questions over the scope of charges.
Among the key concerns raised during the court's fifth status conference on Monday, November 2, was an ICC decision that could limit the killings covered by the case, potentially excluding some victims from the proceedings.
The conference also addressed preparations for Duterte's trial, scheduled to open on November 30, including witness protection measures and arrangements for victims' participation.
In an interview, attorney Kristina Conti, an ICC Assistant to Counsel, said these issues remain significant for victims as the proceedings approach.
Change in scope of charges raises concerns for victims
Conti said victims' representatives are grappling with the implications of an ICC decision issued on October 9 that appears to limit the scope of killings covered by one of the charges.
The case concerns alleged crimes committed between November 1, 2011, and March 16, 2019, when the Philippines was a member of the ICC. However, the decision reportedly limits the killings covered by one charge to the period between July 1, 2016, and September 30, 2018.
“Yung tinatawag na paglimita ng scope ang problema ngayon ng mga biktima kasi posibleng hindi lahat, eh, pumasok doon sa parameters,” Conti told GMA News Online.
(The limitation of the scope is now a problem for victims because some of them may not fall within the parameters of the case.)
Conti said victims' representatives are still trying to understand the implications of the ruling, arguing that the alleged crimes should be considered within the full period of the Philippines' membership in the ICC.
“Dapat hanggang 2019 na miyembro yung Pilipinas ng ICC. Tapos dapat hanggang 2022 kung kailan tsaka pa lang natapos yung term ni Duterte,” she said.
(It should cover when the Philippines was a member of the ICC, until 2019. And Duterte's term only ended in 2022.)
The potential narrowing of the scope is a concern for victims who fear that not all alleged crimes may be considered in the proceedings.
Participating victims need not testify
Conti clarified that victims participating in the proceedings do not necessarily have to take the witness stand. Their role is to express their views and concerns through their common legal representatives and, potentially, seek reparations if Duterte is convicted.
She stressed that the number of participating victims does not determine the strength of the prosecution's evidence.
“Yung pagliit o paglaki ng bilang na ito ay hindi nakakaapekto directly doon sa kaso or doon sa strength ng evidence. Pero siyempre, ibang tulong din yun na alam ng prosecution, makikita nila na ganito karami ang gustong mag-participate,” she said.
(The increase or decrease in the number of participating victims does not directly affect the case or the strength of the evidence. But, of course, it also helps the prosecution to see how many people want to participate.)
Conti encouraged victims to participate even if they are unwilling or unable to testify, submit affidavits, or recount their experiences in court.
“Pero gusto pa rin sana namin na anyayahan sila na mag-participate. Not necessarily para maging witness, not necessarily para magbigay ng statement na kumbaga affidavit, pero para magbigay ng views and concerns, mga pananaw at mga agam-agam,” she said.
(We still want to encourage them to participate. Not necessarily as witnesses, and not necessarily to submit affidavits, but to share their views and concerns.)
Applications from participating victims will continue to be accepted until the prosecution finishes presenting its evidence, Conti said.
The prosecution has been allotted 150 hours to present its evidence, a phase she estimates could take approximately a year.
Victims' safety and participation
Conti said preparations for the November 30 trial were largely in place, with the court emphasizing protective measures for witnesses who will testify either in person or through audio-visual links.
“Pero yung maganda nga dito na na-emphasize ay yung protective measures para sa witnesses,” she said.
(What was particularly good was the emphasis on protective measures for witnesses.)
These measures could include withholding witnesses' identities and preventing them from appearing on screen if the ICC determines that revealing their identities could put them at risk.
“Posibleng hindi rin natin makita sa screen. Posibleng boses lang ang marinig natin o kaya translated voice,” said Conti.
(We may not even see them on screen. We may hear only their voice, or a translated voice.)
She said protecting victims and witnesses is particularly important given the trauma they may experience when recounting alleged abuses.
Filipino language request faces hurdles
Another issue raised by victims' representatives was the request to use Filipino during portions of the proceedings, particularly when reading statements directly from victims.
Conti said the request was not simply about language preference but about allowing victims to hear their experiences conveyed in their own words.
“Hindi sila magsasalita ng Tagalog simple dahil gusto nila, kundi dahil meron silang i-quote o babasahin na statement diretso directly from the victims,” she said.
(They are not asking to speak in Tagalog simply because they want to, but because they intend to quote or read statements directly from the victims.)
However, the request appears unlikely to be granted, meaning statements would have to be delivered in English or translated.
Conti said this would not affect the legal merits of the case but could influence victims' perception of whether they are genuinely included in the proceedings.
“Pero yung impression lang sa Pilipinas, yung participation ng victims. Kumbaga eh, isinali niyo na nga kami... Pero kailangan pala English dito,” she said.
(But it affects the impression in the Philippines about victims' participation. It's as if we're being told, ‘You've included us, but everything has to be in English.’)
She warned that the English-language requirement could discourage some victims from participating, particularly those without immediate access to lawyers or legal representatives.
“Isa siyang malaking barrier—lalo na sa iba na hindi naman naaabot kaagad nung CLRV o kaya nakakapag-consult agad sa mga abogado, so baka maiwan sila sa proseso o hindi nila maintindihan ang nangyayari.”
(It is a significant barrier, especially for those who cannot immediately reach a common legal representative or consult a lawyer. They could be left behind in the process or may not understand what is happening.)
Duterte's trial is scheduled to begin on November 30. He faces three counts of crimes against humanity in connection with alleged killings during his administration's anti-drug campaign. — BM, GMA News

title: LTO issues SCO against driver who hit pedestrian in Pampanga
content:
The Land Transportation Office (LTO) conducted an investigation to identify the registered owner and designated driver of a private vehicle involved in a dangerous driving incident at Hacienda Superclub, Angeles City, Pampanga on November 1, 2026, wherein one individual was hit and several others were put in danger.
After identifying the registered owner and the designated driver, the LTO issued a Show Cause Order (SCO) seeking their explanation regarding the incident.
They were then ordered to appear before the Intelligence and Investigation Division (IID) of the LTO Central Office on November 6, 2026, to attend the hearing and submit a sworn statement, along with relevant documents to support their case.
The violations listed in the SCO include Reckless Driving and Improper Person to Operate a Motor Vehicle, which may be grounds for suspension or revocation of the driver’s license.
In the meantime, the vehicle in question has been placed on alarm status while the designated driver has also been ordered to immediately surrender his IID license, which will be subject to a 90-day preventive suspension.
“Lagi kong sinasabi na makararating at makararating sa LTO ang bawat paglabag, lalo na ang mga insidenteng nagdudulot ng panganib sa publiko. Hindi namin ito palalampasin, at inaasahan naming haharap sa aming tanggapan ang mga sangkot upang ipaliwanag ang kanilang panig at sumunod sa itinakdang proseso,” said LTO Assistant Secretary Markus V. Lacanilao.
(I always say that every violation will reach and will reach the LTO, especially incidents that pose a danger to the public. We will not ignore this, and we expect those involved to appear before our office to explain their side and follow the established process.)
The LTO reiterates that having a license is not only proof that a person is qualified to drive, but it also carries with it the responsibility to be careful and ensure that other people are not put at risk.
"Every motorist is expected to obey traffic laws and use the road with discipline, caution, and respect for others at all times," the agency said. — BAP, GMA News

title: PUV operators summoned over alleged refusal of Libreng Sakay in Cebu City
content:
The Land Transportation Franchising and Regulatory Board (LTFRB) has issued show cause orders to two public utility jeepney operators whose vehicles allegedly refused to pick up passengers under the "Libreng Sakay" (free ride) program during peak travel hours in Cebu City.
In a social media post on Monday, the Department of Transportation (DOTr) said the show cause orders were issued upon the directive of Secretary Vince Dizon.
Based on the show cause orders attached to the post, the jeepneys of both operators were supposed to participate in the government’s Libreng Sakay program along the 01K route, which connects V. Urgello Street.
“Respondent, operating along the 01K route, allegedly refused to take in passengers waiting at a designated bus stop in Mabolo, Cebu City, despite the growing number of commuters waiting for transport during rush hour,” the documents read.
The documents stated that the refusal to convey passengers without just cause—especially for vehicles participating in the Libreng Sakay program—constitutes a violation of “Refusal to Render Public Service/Refusal to Convey Passengers” under existing LTFRB rules and regulations.
The LTFRB directed the operators to submit a written explanation within five days of receiving the order, stating why their Certificate of Public Convenience or Provisional Authority should not be suspended or revoked, and why administrative fines should not be imposed against them.
The operators were also required to submit several supporting documents.
The respondents and the concerned drivers were ordered to appear in person during a formal hearing scheduled for November 12, 2026. — Lyjah Tiffany Bonzo/BM, GMA News

title: PAGASA sees 1-2 tropical cyclones in PAR in November 2026
content:
One or two tropical cyclones are expected to enter or form within the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) in November 2026, according to the state weather bureau PAGASA.
In a report on Balitanghali on Monday, PAGASA noted that historically, tropical cyclones entering in November typically make landfall over the Bicol Region, Eastern Visayas, or the Caraga Region.
Forecast tracks indicate that these tropical cyclones may also traverse the Visayas toward Palawan or cut across Central Luzon, though there remains a chance they could recurve or veer away without making landfall.
Earlier, PAGASA stated that up to four tropical cyclones could still enter or form inside the PAR before the end of 2026, while two or more tropical cyclones may enter between January and April 2027.
According to the bureau’s climate outlook, most parts of the Philippines are expected to experience way below-to-below-normal rainfall in November 2026, except for Davao City, Davao del Norte, and Agusan del Norte, where near-normal rainfall conditions are expected.
From December 2026 through January 2027, PAGASA forecasts way below-to-below-normal rainfall across the country.
El Niño
The effects of a strong El Niño are expected to prevail across the country toward the end of 2026 and persist into the first quarter of 2027.
According to PAGASA, at least 12 areas in the Philippines are forecast to experience drought this November as the strong El Niño persists.
While El Niño is typically associated with dry conditions and hot weather, the state weather bureau explained that historically, more tropical cyclones reach typhoon or super typhoon intensity during El Niño events, regardless of whether the phenomenon is classified as weak, moderate, strong, or very strong.
PAGASA Climate Monitoring and Prediction Section Chief Ana Liza Solis explained that warmer ocean temperatures could still create favorable conditions for tropical cyclone development.
“Dahil napakainit nga po ng temperatura ng karagatan na pinagmumulan ng mga tropical cyclone development, so favorable pa rin po siya na magkaroon ng mga bagyo and historically po, ang mga possible po ay mga typhoon and super typhoon category,” Solis said.
(Because the seas where tropical cyclones develop are very warm, conditions remain favorable for cyclone development, and historically, typhoons and super typhoons are possible.)
Solis noted that El Niño does not eliminate the possibility of rain.–NB, GMA News

title: Oil drops as US midterm caution prevails
content:
European stocks edged down on Monday after Friday’s tech rout, with investors looking ahead to Apple’s earnings and taking comfort from a sharp fall in oil prices amid hopes for a deal to end the Iran war.
Markets face a pivotal week, with investors digesting the Federal Reserve's and the European Central Bank’s latest policy decisions, earnings season in full swing and the US midterm elections on Tuesday.
Euro zone government bonds were slightly lower after last week's rally, while investor sentiment remained fragile amid concerns over France's fiscal outlook and continuing street unrest.
MSCI's main world stocks index was roughly unchanged, while Europe's STOXX 600 was down 0.10%, with tech stocks rising 0.30%.
Nasdaq futures climbed 0.73% and S&P 500 futures increased 0.42%. The S&P 500 index fell 1.82% on Friday, while the Nasdaq tumbled 2.86%.
Brent crude futures fell 4.5% to about $108 as Iranian negotiators have left talks with Qatari mediators and a draft proposal is being circulated with a follow-up meeting possible. US President Donald Trump recently threatened new attacks against Iran.
Investors remain cautious ahead of the US vote, with European stock markets facing a different set of challenges from their US counterparts.
"Further expected downside for the euro area PMI is a drag on our Stoxx 600 forecast trajectory," wrote Sebastian Raedler, head of European equity strategy at BofA.
"However, the main reason for our caution on European equities is the risk of disappointment in the AI capex cycle as AI models commodities and competitive moats prove limited."
While earnings outlooks remained in focus, investors expect US equities to come under pressure in the event of a Democratic sweep, as markets price in the risk of higher corporate taxes and tighter AI regulation.
Opinion polls suggest Democrats are favored to win the House, while the Senate remains too close to call, leaving the party well short of a veto-proof two-thirds majority.
"The combination of deteriorating cash flows and rising capital commitments means the debate over whether AI returns can ultimately justify the scale of investment may not be resolved anytime soon," Emmanuel Cau, head of European equity strategy at Barclays, said.
Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, CEO remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six quarters.
Goldman Sachs analysts expect capital spending by hyperscalers to nearly double to $800 billion this year and rise further to $1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth slowing to 18% next year from nearly 30% in 2026.
"The next phase will be less about identifying who is exposed to AI and more about distinguishing who is already converting that demand into cash, who is still funding the build-out, and what valuation investors are being asked to pay for each," Kristofer Barrett, head of global equities at Carmignac, said.
US dollar safe-haven status under scrutiny
In foreign exchange markets, major currencies were largely subdued. The euro rose 0.46% to $1.1199, while the dollar was up 0.16% at 157.90 yen JPY=EBS.
Rising oil prices tend to hurt the euro and yen as they worsen the outlook for energy-importing economies.
Investors are also questioning the dollar's safe-haven status, concerned that a renewed tech-driven market selloff could weaken the US currency.
George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, said the US's reliance on foreign equity inflows was historically unprecedented and evidence showed that when the source of an equity shock is US-centric the dollar-equity correlation flips to positive.
Among central banks meeting this week, markets are pricing in rate increases from the Reserve Bank of Australia, Bank of England and Riksbank, while the Norges Bank is seen on hold.
Data due this week include the US ISM manufacturing survey for October later on Monday and the closely watched non-farm payrolls report on Friday. — Reuters

title: Kiko Pangilinan urges crackdown on hoarders, profiteers amid El Niño threat
content:
Senate Agriculture Committee chair Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan on Monday urged government agencies to intensify their crackdown on hoarding and profiteering as the looming Super El Niño threatens food production and prices.
In a statement, Pangilinan said enforcement of existing laws, particularly Republic Act No. 7581 or the Price Act, should not be limited to small vendors but should also target major business operators and those behind illegal price manipulation.
“I call on implementing agencies, local price councils, and law enforcement authorities to gather evidence and pursue criminal and administrative cases, where warranted, against those responsible for illegal price manipulation,” Pangilinan said.
“Kung maliliit na tindero lamang ang hahabulin, walang saysay ito. Dapat nating panagutin ang mga malalaking negosyante, mga may-ari, at mga utak sa likod ng mga sindikatong sangkot sa hoarding at manipulasyon ng presyo,” he added.
(If we only go after small-scale vendors, it’s pointless. We must hold major business owners, proprietors, and the masterminds behind syndicates involved in hoarding and price manipulation accountable.)
Section 5 of the Price Act prohibits hoarding, profiteering, and the formation of cartels involving basic necessities and prime commodities.
Violators face imprisonment of five to 15 years and a fine ranging from P5,000 to P2 million.
Pangilinan also urged the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Health (DOH), and the Price Coordinating Council to strengthen market monitoring and enforce price freezes in areas placed under a state of calamity due to El Niño.
“Hindi na dapat pagkakitaan ang nalalapit na kalamidad na magpapahirap pa lalo sa ating mga kababayan, lalo na sa mga magsasaka at mangingisda na mamimili rin sa palengke. Sa panahon ng krisis, dapat protektado ang mga mamimili laban sa pagsasamantala,” he said.
(We should not profit from the impending calamity that will further burden our countrymen, especially farmers and fisherfolk who also buy food at the market. In times of crisis, consumers must be protected from exploitation.)
Section 6 of the Price Act provides for an automatic price freeze on basic necessities at their prevailing prices when an area is placed under a state of calamity or emergency, among other circumstances.
Unless lifted earlier by the President, the price freeze remains in effect for the duration of the condition that triggered it, but for no more than 60 days.— MCG, GMA News

title: Binance sees outflows stabilizing as exchange returns online after $6.3 billion heist
content:
Binance customers pulled $3.64 billion, or 2.1% of its assets, as the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange resumed service after a security breach linked to North Korea saw $6.3 billion stolen from the platform last week.
The exchange moved to reassure crypto investors and said withdrawals were stabilizing after an initial spike and deposit volumes had remained "substantial" after, what analysts believe, may be the world's biggest financial robbery ever.
After hitting a six-week low on Friday, bitcoin BTC= prices recovered slightly through the weekend to trade above $78,000 on Monday. Ether ETH= hit a two-month low on Friday and also recovered a little to $2,287.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally. It said on Sunday it had $171 billion in total assets under management as of October 28.
The Binance theft adds to a string of recent crypto thefts. Attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 incidents last year, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
Withdrawal levels are an early test of whether customers still trust Binance with their money after the attack. The exchange said it had covered 95% of the assets stolen in the heist.
Stablecoin market capitalizations tend to fall when money is leaving cryptocurrencies and they have dropped since Friday. The combined capitalization of the two largest stablecoins, USDT and USDC, has dropped by about $1.2 billion since Friday, according to Coinmarketcap.com.
Spot bitcoin ETFs shed $643 million on Friday, the largest daily outflow of October, and more than $1.3 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs.
"I get why, for conservative institutional investors, this is unsettling," Redbord said.
"A hack at a financial institution means stolen usernames and passwords. A hack at a crypto exchange is bank robbery at the speed of the internet, which creates an unstable risk profile for anyone responsible for other people’s capital."
Phased withdrawals
Binance said on Sunday it had covered $6 billion of stolen cryptocurrencies by using its money to buy replacement tokens. The remaining 5% of stolen tokens consist of less liquid assets and may take longer to source, it said.
Despite those measures, some users were weighing options to hedge risks.
Jay Koh, vice president at the Asia Web3 AI Association, said he had not withdrawn any of his holdings from Binance, as most of his funds were held in a cold wallet, which was not impacted by the hack.
"I would not necessarily withdraw everything from Binance ... However, I do think it is prudent to review exposure, diversify custody arrangements and avoid keeping more assets on any single platform than necessary."
Binance, which was founded in China, said the rollout for withdrawals would be carried out in stages, prioritizing user demand. The first phase covered 15 tokens including bitcoin, ether and those involving some USDC and USDT stablecoins and dogecoin.
"We are taking a phased approach by prioritizing tokens based on the past week data of user demand," Binance said in an earlier article posted on X.
It added, "Rest assured that market conditions are stable."
Binance said the net outflows reflected what clients had withdrawn and deposited after the event.
Crypto analytics platform DefiLlama said on its dashboard that outflows were higher, at $5.81 billion, up from the $4.36 billion it showed earlier. Binance did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the updated figures.
"This figure does not contain the flows we have deposited to our own new hot wallet, so they are not accurate. Our last update on X is closest to accurate (outstanding the moves in both deposits and withdrawals since it was posted)," a spokesperson for Binance said of the initial DefiLlama data.
FBI ties attack to North Korean unit
The FBI said on Saturday that the North Korean state-sponsored unit known as TraderTraitor was responsible for the attack.
Pyongyang has for years denied using state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue generation. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.
Law enforcement observed members of the unit converting stolen assets into the cryptocurrency ether, the FBI said in a statement, adding that it expected "further laundering" of the assets through the use of related technology.
Analysts had also pointed to North Korea's involvement. The bulk of the theft unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
US President Donald Trump, however, later on Saturday said it remained unclear whether North Korea was involved.
"We don't know if it's North Korea — but if it is, we'll talk to North Korea about it," Trump told reporters in comments posted by a White House account on X. —Reuters

title: WTO flags high trade costs, regulatory hurdles in PH
content:
GENEVA, SWITZERLAND — The Philippines needs to address non-tariff barriers to reduce trade costs and strengthen its competitiveness in global supply chains, including the semiconductor industry, World Trade Organization (WTO) Secretariat officials said.
Asked which reforms the Philippines should prioritize, a WTO official identified non-tariff barriers, such as import licensing and labeling requirements, which can increase the cost of trade and doing business in the country.
“Non-tariff barriers, I would say,” the official said, noting, however, that the Philippines had already made progress in investment and tariff reforms.
The official added that the Philippine government would ultimately decide which reforms to prioritize.
The recommendation comes as the WTO Secretariat’s 2026 Trade Policy Review: Philippines cited estimates showing that the country's trade costs are 20% higher than the ASEAN average.
WTO data show that the country's simple average most-favored-nation (MFN) applied tariff rate stood at 5.9% in 2025, with only 13.6% of imports entering duty-free under MFN terms. Its trade-weighted MFN average was 6% in 2024.
Other measures that add to trade costs include pre-border technical verification, cross-border electronic invoicing and a national single window that has yet to become fully operational, according to the officials.
They also cited fragmented regulations and logistics pass-through fees, partly attributable to the country's geography and 7,641 islands, as factors that could drive up trade costs. However, they cautioned against interpreting the figures as an indication that the Philippines was falling behind its regional peers.
“Lowering costs and making the economy more attractive to do business with is work for any country,” another official said in an interview at WTO headquarters.
The official also said the Philippines could benefit from strengthening industry clusters and training workers for semiconductor-related jobs to deepen its participation in global value chains.
The country could also capitalize on its strength in services exports, particularly business process management services.
“You need to specialize, so you specialize in what you're good at. The Philippines is good at providing services, and definitely that's how you earn your money. But at the same time, the Philippines has definitely more than services,” the official said.
For his part, Philippine Ambassador and Permanent Representative to the WTO Manuel Antonio Teehankee said the country should address infrastructure and logistics concerns to help reduce trade costs.
“Improved infrastructure for inter-island transport and rail is very important for moving goods inside the country because import-export is also dependent on internal logistics and warehousing. So that's the other big area of infrastructure that we should develop,” he said in a separate interview.
Latest data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) show that net inflows of foreign direct investments (FDI) stood at US$689 million in July, down 44.1% from US$1.23 billion in the same month last year but up 54.1% from the US$447 million recorded in June.
Meanwhile, the Board of Investments (BOI) approved P900.06 billion worth of investments from January to September, up 53.05% from the same period last year and equivalent to 90% of its P1-trillion target for the year.
Domestic investors accounted for 89.88%, or P808.96 billion, of the approved investments, while foreign investors accounted for P90.40 billion.
The Philippines is also seeking to capitalize on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with the country set to host the US-led Pax Silica hub on a 1,600-hectare site within the 9,450-hectare New Clark City in Tarlac. The initiative is part of efforts to build an allied supply-chain network for critical technologies and minerals.
The country is also eyeing Bulacan as a gateway to consolidate components sourced from across the region, assemble them into AI computing hardware, including server racks, and ship the finished products to global markets. — MCG, GMA News

title: WTO chief urges PH, ASEAN to diversify trade beyond US, China
content:
GENEVA, Switzerland — The Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) should diversify their trade markets and shift away from heavy reliance on the United States for exports and China for supplies, a top official of the World Trade Organization (WTO) said.
According to WTO director-general Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Philippines and its Southeast Asian neighbors should explore trading opportunities beyond traditional partners, including Africa, Central Asia, and Latin America, to broaden their trading relationships.
“The problem, the issue with ASEAN is they are highly dependent on the US market. Highly. So my message to ASEAN is diversify, diversify, diversify,” she told reporters in a briefing at the WTO headquarters.
“You know, you have many Asians who are in Latin America. You have a huge Japanese population in Brazil and in Peru. You have Filipinos everywhere, so why are you not (diversifying?)” she added.
Okonjo-Iweala also cited trading opportunities in Africa, which Thailand has included in its long-term plans because of the continent’s growing labor force, as well as in resource-rich Central Asian countries such as Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in Central Asia, and Armenia, and Azerbaijan in South Caucasus.
The Philippines’ reliance on major trading partners is seen in the latest trade figures, as the United States accounted for more than a quarter or 26.6% of exports in September, while South Korea and China together accounted for nearly half or 48.4% of imports, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).
Total trade in goods for the month reached $24.903 billion in September, with imports exceeding exports by $5.154 billion. The latest trade gap compares with the $4.293-billion deficit in August, and the $4.672-billion deficit in September 2025.
The areas cited by Okonjo-Iweala — Africa, Central Asia, and Latin America — were not among the Philippines’ leading trade partners in September, highlighting the potential to expand into such markets.
“My message to them (ASEAN) is to diversify your market supplies because you’re very dependent on China. Diversify your market for your goods because you’re very dependent on the US,” she said.
Her remarks come a month before the Philippines is set to host the 49th ASEAN Summit, with US President Donald Trump confirmed to attend.
The WTO has upgraded its outlook for Asian trade this year, based on its Global Trade Outlook and Statistics report in October. It expects Asia’s merchandise export volume to grow by 9.9% this year, up from its March forecast of 3.5%.
Should this be realized, it will mark the third straight year of acceleration after the 8.3% in 2024, and 9.6% in 2025.
“With our forecast in March, we had seen record growth in AI (artificial intelligence) deals on goods trade in 2025, and we though that the pace of investment might moderate in 2026. It hasn’t only not moderated, it’s accelerated,” WTO chief of forecasting Coleman Nee said at a separate briefing.
“Growth in AI-enabling goods has been even stronger than expected, and that’s the main impetus behind that. The other thing is economies have been more resilient to rising energy prices than perhaps many expected,” he added.
For 2027, however, the WTO expects Asian merchandise trade volume growth to decelerate to 5.2%, but still faster than the 3.2% forecast made in March.
“When you have above-average growth in one year, it tends to be somewhat weaker the next year. There’s a lot of uncertainty about 2027 generally, just because of energy prices and the durability of the AI investment boom,” Nee said.
“It could go on for several years. The Middle East conflict could be resolved tomorrow. We don’t have a crystal ball. These are probabilistic estimates based on data available at the moment,” he added.
The Philippines is looking to capitalize on the AI boom, as it is set to host the US-led Pax Silica hub in a 1,600-hectare site within the 9,450-hecyare New Clark City. It is in line with efforts to build a network of allied supply chains for critical technologies and minerals.
The country is also eyeing Bulacan as a gateway for consolidating components sourced from across the region, assembling them into AI compute hardware, including server racks, and shipping the finished products to global markets. — RSJ, GMA News

"The combination of deteriorating cash flows and rising capital commitments means the debate over whether AI returns can ultimately justify the scale of investment may not be resolved anytime soon," Emmanuel Cau, head of European equity strategy at Barclays, said.
Apple will face scrutiny over three key issues: its crucial holiday-quarter outlook, CEO remarks on AI and the revamped Siri, and rising memory-chip costs that analysts expect to drag quarterly profit growth to its weakest in six quarters.
Goldman Sachs analysts expect capital spending by hyperscalers to nearly double to $800 billion this year and rise further to $1.2 trillion in 2027. At the same time, they see S&P 500 earnings per share growth slowing to 18% next year from nearly 30% in 2026.
"The next phase will be less about identifying who is exposed to AI and more about distinguishing who is already converting that demand into cash, who is still funding the build-out, and what valuation investors are being asked to pay for each," Kristofer Barrett, head of global equities at Carmignac, said.
US dollar safe-haven status under scrutiny
In foreign exchange markets, major currencies were largely subdued. The euro rose 0.46% to $1.1199, while the dollar was up 0.16% at 157.90 yen JPY=EBS.
Rising oil prices tend to hurt the euro and yen as they worsen the outlook for energy-importing economies.
Investors are also questioning the dollar's safe-haven status, concerned that a renewed tech-driven market selloff could weaken the US currency.
George Saravelos, global head of forex strategy at Deutsche Bank, said the US's reliance on foreign equity inflows was historically unprecedented and evidence showed that when the source of an equity shock is US-centric the dollar-equity correlation flips to positive.
Among central banks meeting this week, markets are pricing in rate increases from the Reserve Bank of Australia, Bank of England and Riksbank, while the Norges Bank is seen on hold.
Data due this week include the US ISM manufacturing survey for October later on Monday and the closely watched non-farm payrolls report on Friday. — Reuters

title: Kiko Pangilinan urges crackdown on hoarders, profiteers amid El Niño threat
content:
Senate Agriculture Committee chair Francis “Kiko” Pangilinan on Monday urged government agencies to intensify their crackdown on hoarding and profiteering as the looming Super El Niño threatens food production and prices.
In a statement, Pangilinan said enforcement of existing laws, particularly Republic Act No. 7581 or the Price Act, should not be limited to small vendors but should also target major business operators and those behind illegal price manipulation.
“I call on implementing agencies, local price councils, and law enforcement authorities to gather evidence and pursue criminal and administrative cases, where warranted, against those responsible for illegal price manipulation,” Pangilinan said.
“Kung maliliit na tindero lamang ang hahabulin, walang saysay ito. Dapat nating panagutin ang mga malalaking negosyante, mga may-ari, at mga utak sa likod ng mga sindikatong sangkot sa hoarding at manipulasyon ng presyo,” he added.
(If we only go after small-scale vendors, it’s pointless. We must hold major business owners, proprietors, and the masterminds behind syndicates involved in hoarding and price manipulation accountable.)
Section 5 of the Price Act prohibits hoarding, profiteering, and the formation of cartels involving basic necessities and prime commodities.
Violators face imprisonment of five to 15 years and a fine ranging from P5,000 to P2 million.
Pangilinan also urged the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI), Department of Agriculture (DA), Department of Health (DOH), and the Price Coordinating Council to strengthen market monitoring and enforce price freezes in areas placed under a state of calamity due to El Niño.
“Hindi na dapat pagkakitaan ang nalalapit na kalamidad na magpapahirap pa lalo sa ating mga kababayan, lalo na sa mga magsasaka at mangingisda na mamimili rin sa palengke. Sa panahon ng krisis, dapat protektado ang mga mamimili laban sa pagsasamantala,” he said.
(We should not profit from the impending calamity that will further burden our countrymen, especially farmers and fisherfolk who also buy food at the market. In times of crisis, consumers must be protected from exploitation.)
Section 6 of the Price Act provides for an automatic price freeze on basic necessities at their prevailing prices when an area is placed under a state of calamity or emergency, among other circumstances.
Unless lifted earlier by the President, the price freeze remains in effect for the duration of the condition that triggered it, but for no more than 60 days.— MCG, GMA News

title: WTO flags high trade costs, regulatory hurdles in PH
content:
GENEVA, SWITZERLAND — The Philippines needs to address non-tariff barriers to reduce trade costs and strengthen its competitiveness in global supply chains, including the semiconductor industry, World Trade Organization (WTO) Secretariat officials said.
Asked which reforms the Philippines should prioritize, a WTO official identified non-tariff barriers, such as import licensing and labeling requirements, which can increase the cost of trade and doing business in the country.
“Non-tariff barriers, I would say,” the official said, noting, however, that the Philippines had already made progress in investment and tariff reforms.
The official added that the Philippine government would ultimately decide which reforms to prioritize.
The recommendation comes as the WTO Secretariat’s 2026 Trade Policy Review: Philippines cited estimates showing that the country's trade costs are 20% higher than the ASEAN average.
WTO data show that the country's simple average most-favored-nation (MFN) applied tariff rate stood at 5.9% in 2025, with only 13.6% of imports entering duty-free under MFN terms. Its trade-weighted MFN average was 6% in 2024.
Other measures that add to trade costs include pre-border technical verification, cross-border electronic invoicing and a national single window that has yet to become fully operational, according to the officials.
They also cited fragmented regulations and logistics pass-through fees, partly attributable to the country's geography and 7,641 islands, as factors that could drive up trade costs. However, they cautioned against interpreting the figures as an indication that the Philippines was falling behind its regional peers.
“Lowering costs and making the economy more attractive to do business with is work for any country,” another official said in an interview at WTO headquarters.
The official also said the Philippines could benefit from strengthening industry clusters and training workers for semiconductor-related jobs to deepen its participation in global value chains.
The country could also capitalize on its strength in services exports, particularly business process management services.
“You need to specialize, so you specialize in what you're good at. The Philippines is good at providing services, and definitely that's how you earn your money. But at the same time, the Philippines has definitely more than services,” the official said.
For his part, Philippine Ambassador and Permanent Representative to the WTO Manuel Antonio Teehankee said the country should address infrastructure and logistics concerns to help reduce trade costs.
“Improved infrastructure for inter-island transport and rail is very important for moving goods inside the country because import-export is also dependent on internal logistics and warehousing. So that's the other big area of infrastructure that we should develop,” he said in a separate interview.
Latest data from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) show that net inflows of foreign direct investments (FDI) stood at US$689 million in July, down 44.1% from US$1.23 billion in the same month last year but up 54.1% from the US$447 million recorded in June.
Meanwhile, the Board of Investments (BOI) approved P900.06 billion worth of investments from January to September, up 53.05% from the same period last year and equivalent to 90% of its P1-trillion target for the year.
Domestic investors accounted for 89.88%, or P808.96 billion, of the approved investments, while foreign investors accounted for P90.40 billion.
The Philippines is also seeking to capitalize on the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, with the country set to host the US-led Pax Silica hub on a 1,600-hectare site within the 9,450-hectare New Clark City in Tarlac. The initiative is part of efforts to build an allied supply-chain network for critical technologies and minerals.
The country is also eyeing Bulacan as a gateway to consolidate components sourced from across the region, assemble them into AI computing hardware, including server racks, and ship the finished products to global markets. — MCG, GMA News

title: WTO chief urges PH, ASEAN to diversify trade beyond US, China
content:
GENEVA, Switzerland — The Philippines and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) should diversify their trade markets and shift away from heavy reliance on the United States for exports and China for supplies, a top official of the World Trade Organization (WTO) said.
According to WTO director-general Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, the Philippines and its Southeast Asian neighbors should explore trading opportunities beyond traditional partners, including Africa, Central Asia, and Latin America, to broaden their trading relationships.
“The problem, the issue with ASEAN is they are highly dependent on the US market. Highly. So my message to ASEAN is diversify, diversify, diversify,” she told reporters in a briefing at the WTO headquarters.
“You know, you have many Asians who are in Latin America. You have a huge Japanese population in Brazil and in Peru. You have Filipinos everywhere, so why are you not (diversifying?)” she added.
Okonjo-Iweala also cited trading opportunities in Africa, which Thailand has included in its long-term plans because of the continent’s growing labor force, as well as in resource-rich Central Asian countries such as Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan in Central Asia, and Armenia, and Azerbaijan in South Caucasus.
The Philippines’ reliance on major trading partners is seen in the latest trade figures, as the United States accounted for more than a quarter or 26.6% of exports in September, while South Korea and China together accounted for nearly half or 48.4% of imports, according to the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA).
Total trade in goods for the month reached $24.903 billion in September, with imports exceeding exports by $5.154 billion. The latest trade gap compares with the $4.293-billion deficit in August, and the $4.672-billion deficit in September 2025.
The areas cited by Okonjo-Iweala — Africa, Central Asia, and Latin America — were not among the Philippines’ leading trade partners in September, highlighting the potential to expand into such markets.
“My message to them (ASEAN) is to diversify your market supplies because you’re very dependent on China. Diversify your market for your goods because you’re very dependent on the US,” she said.
Her remarks come a month before the Philippines is set to host the 49th ASEAN Summit, with US President Donald Trump confirmed to attend.
The WTO has upgraded its outlook for Asian trade this year, based on its Global Trade Outlook and Statistics report in October. It expects Asia’s merchandise export volume to grow by 9.9% this year, up from its March forecast of 3.5%.
Should this be realized, it will mark the third straight year of acceleration after the 8.3% in 2024, and 9.6% in 2025.
“With our forecast in March, we had seen record growth in AI (artificial intelligence) deals on goods trade in 2025, and we though that the pace of investment might moderate in 2026. It hasn’t only not moderated, it’s accelerated,” WTO chief of forecasting Coleman Nee said at a separate briefing.
“Growth in AI-enabling goods has been even stronger than expected, and that’s the main impetus behind that. The other thing is economies have been more resilient to rising energy prices than perhaps many expected,” he added.
For 2027, however, the WTO expects Asian merchandise trade volume growth to decelerate to 5.2%, but still faster than the 3.2% forecast made in March.
“When you have above-average growth in one year, it tends to be somewhat weaker the next year. There’s a lot of uncertainty about 2027 generally, just because of energy prices and the durability of the AI investment boom,” Nee said.
“It could go on for several years. The Middle East conflict could be resolved tomorrow. We don’t have a crystal ball. These are probabilistic estimates based on data available at the moment,” he added.
The Philippines is looking to capitalize on the AI boom, as it is set to host the US-led Pax Silica hub in a 1,600-hectare site within the 9,450-hecyare New Clark City. It is in line with efforts to build a network of allied supply chains for critical technologies and minerals.
The country is also eyeing Bulacan as a gateway for consolidating components sourced from across the region, assembling them into AI compute hardware, including server racks, and shipping the finished products to global markets. — RSJ, GMA News

title: Study: Grads earn more when jobs match academic training
content:
Study: Grads earn more when jobs match academic training
MANILA, Philippines — Graduates tend to earn more when their jobs match their academic training, according to a study conducted by the Philippine Institute for Development Studies.
The PIDS study – Labor Market Outcomes of Education Graduates in the Philippines: The Role of Licensure Credentials and Job Matching – also showed that licensure alone was not significantly associated with higher wages.
It is authored by PIDS research specialist Anna Rita Vargas, research analyst Paola Ellaine Luzon and senior research fellow Connie Bayudan-Dacuycuy, who examined the labor market outcomes of Filipinos aged 22 to 60 with bachelor’s degrees in education science and related fields.
Using data from the July 2024 round of the merged Labor Force Survey-Annual Poverty Indicators Survey, the researchers analyzed outcomes among education graduates with or without professional licenses.
The study’s weighted estimates represented approximately 1.83 million graduates nationwide.
The authors said among licensed graduates, the predicted probability of underemployment was 3.98 percent for those in public-sector employment, compared with 14.73 percent for those in private-sector employment or who are self-employed.
The researchers recommended aligning curricula and licensure preparation with labor market needs and strengthening career pathways for licensed and unlicensed education graduates.
The PIDS added that the relationship between licensure and wages also varies by employment sector.
In particular, the results suggest that the financial benefits associated with licensure differ between those employed in government or government-controlled corporations and those working elsewhere.
“These findings mean that having a professional license does not automatically translate into higher pay. While a license can demonstrate professional qualifications and help graduates qualify for certain jobs, their earnings also depend on whether their work matches their training and the sector in which they are employed. The study identifies these relationships but does not establish that licensure or working in a particular sector directly causes higher earnings,” the study said.

Philippines to host Quad leaders’ summit during ASEAN meet
MANILA, Philippines — The leaders of Australia, India, Japan and the United States will meet in Manila during the Nov. 15-18 Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) conference, the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue’s first leaders’ summit since 2024, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio confirmed.
The summit would be the first for US President Donald Trump in his current term.
“We will have a Quad leaders’ meeting in Manila in the – I guess today is the 31st – next month,” Rubio said on Saturday on the sidelines of the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia.
The Philippines chairs the ASEAN this year and will host the leaders’ summit and other meetings from Nov. 16 to 18.
The Quad group is a key strategic partnership for cooperation on maritime security. It aims to promote a “free and open” Indo-Pacific and balance China’s expanding military and economic influence in the area.
During the G20 gathering, Rubio said the world is seeing concerning attacks in the South China Sea and the Strait of Taiwan that put economies in danger.
He stressed that one of the most severe consequences to sea lanes being under attack or under coercion is the rise of food security problems.
The foreign ministers of Quad nations remain seriously concerned about the situation in the East China Sea and the South China Sea and the militarization of disputed features.
In a statement during the Quad Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in New Delhi in May, the Quad reiterated its strong opposition to any destabilizing or unilateral actions, including by force or coercion, that threaten peace and stability in the region.
Ironclad
Meanwhile, US Ambassador Lee Lipton described Washington’s commitment to Philippine security as “ironclad,” following the visit of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Cebu last week.
Lipton said Hegseth’s leadership of the Department of War and his frequent engagements with the US’s partners in Southeast Asia demonstrate the Trump administration’s determination to strengthen alliances, deepen regional cooperation and ensure that peace is backed by strength.
“As we mark 75 years of the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty, our message is clear: our alliance is stronger than ever,” Lipton said. “We stand firmly with the Filipino people in defending sovereignty, protecting territorial integrity and upholding the freedom of navigation on which we all rely for vibrant global commerce.”

title: DepEd prioritizes violence-hit campuses in hiring counselor associates

DepEd prioritizes violence-hit campuses in hiring counselor associates
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Education (DepEd) is conducting risk assessments to prioritize large schools and those with a history of violence in the hiring and deployment of school counselor associates amid budget constraints, Education Secretary Sonny Angara said.
“Every year we are given a budget for the hiring of counselor associates. We distribute it for the 40,000-plus schools based on risk and usually, we have a risk assessment. Usually, incidents of bullying and violence tend to happen in bigger schools, in schools in urban areas. So, those schools that have a history, we will really provide them counselor associates,” Angara said.
The DepEd aims to complete the hiring of 10,000 school counselor associates by the end of 2026.
Angara noted that only 5,000 of the more than 45,000 schools nationwide have registered guidance counselors.
“What we hope is that we hire a combination of guidance counselors and have school counselor associates. Not a full-fledged guidance counselor, but with experience or units in psychology, in behavioral science, so will be able to spot any mental health issues and be able to guide our students,” he added.
Angara said the hiring is timely amid increasing incidents of bullying, school violence, mental health issues and depression among learners.
The DepEd is also seeking an additional P147.9 billion from the Senate to fund important programs left unfunded under its proposed P975.96-billion allocation for 2027.
“If you look at the most successful countries with the most successful education systems, they tend to spend more on education,” Angara said.
He admitted, however, that securing the additional funding would be a long shot.
“It is a long shot… but it’s a shot we have to take because it’s our duty. I think the fact that the senators are asking what are the most important items for us, I think that’s an indication that they really want to, at least at a minimum level, restore some of the budget that was taken away and fund other programs that may not be funded anymore,” he added.
